Synopsis:
    German exports fell 0.8% in July 2026, missing expectations of a +0.1% rise. Weakness was driven by declines in EU-bound shipments (-1.6%) and exports to China (-9.5%). Exports to the US surged +19.1%, partially offsetting the broader decline. Imports dropped sharply (-5.7%), pushing the trade surplus to €21.3bn. Exporter sentiment has improved, with Ifo expectations at their highest since pre-Ukraine war levels. However, Germany faces structural competitive pressure from Chinese rivals, particularly in high-tech sectors, while Chinese exports surged +25% YoY in August. The overall picture remains one of fragile, volatile recovery.

Risk score: 30 — Germany's trade fragility and China competitive pressure are well-flagged themes; the specific July data miss and the magnitude of the US export surge add some incremental surprise, but the broader narrative is not new.
